newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian money rates ease, few see Dutch rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Belgian money rates ease, few see Dutch rate hike.

text.p: Belgian money rates extended Wednesday's slight recovery on Thursday despite some talk the Dutch central bank could raise its special advances rate this afternoon (1400 GMT) DNBH.

Dealers said the market was still being helped by the Tuesday's Treasury move to issue fewer new bills than at maturity, thus injecting cash, and also by 20.8 billion francs of coupon payments yesterday on OLO 16.
Dealers dismissed the talk of a Dutch rate hike. If there was one, the National Bank of Belgium NBBY was unlikely to follow, analysts added.
By 0845 GMT, shortly before the Belgian central bank's daily repo operation, one-week repos were at 3.85/94 percent from 3.92/98 late on Wednesday and 3.90/99 on Tuesday.
Three-month Treasury bill yields had eased to 3.57/59 percent from 3.60/63 percent on Wednesday and an average auction level of 3.68 percent on Tuesday.

"People were talking about (a Dutch rate hike) yesterday. Most people I have spoken to today don't expect them to do anything because the currency is a bit better," one T-bill trader said. "I don't think a rate rise would be good for the market."
Kredietbank economist Caroline Ven did not expect the Belgian central bank would follow the Dutch even if there was a rate hike.
Both banks at present have their key money market rates pegged at 3.00 percent, the same as the German repo rate.

"The Dutch economic situation is very different. Growth has been strong for several years. A Dutch rate hike would not cause any problems for the economy whereas in Belgium...it would be pre-emptive in this phase of the business cycle," she said.
Another analyst agreed, adding the NBB would not move before the Bundesbank. "(The NBB) will wait as long as possible."
An OLO trader said a Dutch move could affect the money market but was unlikely to move the long-end, which was being driven by Germany and the U.S.
Belgian bonds would only sell off if second quarter U.S. GDP due to be released this afternoon came in much stronger than the expected 2.0 percent.
"If it's far away we will have a strong reaction, but there are a lot of other figures too, like the PMI, and the non-farm payrolls tomorrow which will be more decisive," he said.
By mid-morning OLOs were flat to lower, lagging a slight upmove in Bunds.
